Alex / Maggie — thanks for a productive session today. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key pain points, goals, and a concise set of technical asks so we can align the POC scope. Attaching a one-pager with the call notes and a rough MOP for the POC.

Topline pain points we heard
- Production latency spikes impacting end-user classification flows; business target is <120ms end-to-end at 95th percentile for single-turn classification. Spikes today often land 200–400ms under load.
- Sustained throughput requirement: ~200 qps per region for core inference path, with short-term bursts up to 500 qps during peak windows.
- Model quality sensitivity: Cliffside needs a local 70B-ish open model for higher accuracy on their domain prompts; embeddings used for similarity must be stable across retrains.
- Compliance: log retention and data residency constraints — some customer data must stay within the US region and be accessible for audit.

Initial technical constraints and priorities
- We should validate 95th percentile E2E (client -> Redwood -> model -> response) under real prompt sets and typical request/response size (avg 450 tokens output).
- Priority is latency, then cost. If needed, we'll evaluate quantized model variants for throughput improvements but will validate quality regressions against Cliffside prompt set.
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated (reserved) pools in us-east and us-west with automatic fallback to hosted variants if capacity is constrained. Private deployment (VPC) remains on the table depending on procurement timeline and contracts.

POC asks from Redwood (what we'd need from Cliffside)
1) A sample of 500 representative inference requests (anonymized) covering the mix of short/long prompts and typical response lengths.
2) A prioritized prompt set (20–30) for accuracy checks and quality gating.
3) Expected SLAs and any strict jitter tolerances for the 95th percentile.
4) A contact in procurement for procurement timeline/standard SOW terms (we copied procurement above).

Next steps (proposed)
- Redwood to deliver an initial topology sketch and SLO baseline (by Tue 5/11).
- Cliffside to share anonymized workload sample and prioritized prompts (by Fri 5/14).
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Rishi to lock GPU sizing and fallback models (propose Wed 5/12).

Attachments: cliffside-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), mop_cliffside_poc_sketch.xlsx (POC MOP draft)

Thanks — Lauren

Subject: Technical feasibility notes / proposed topology (for Cliffside)

Following Lauren's summary and Alex's clarifications, some initial technical notes and a proposed topology for the POC. High-level feasibility looks good; a few trade-offs to flag.

1) Baseline assumptions (to validate on the sample payloads)
- Avg output size: 450 tokens (as noted) — this drives KV cache and batching behavior.
- Typical request context: 2–3 turns, median prompt length ~700 tokens.

2) GPU sizing & expected latency (ballpark)
- For a ~70B dense model (FP16 or quantized to 4-bit), recommended hardware for the Dedicated pool: H100 or A100 80GB class nodes with model parallelism.
- Expected per-token generation time (single request, no aggressive batching): ~4–6 ms/token on H100 for well-optimized kernels. For a 450-token response this maps to ~1.8–2.7s purely model compute — but in practice we must consider streaming and overlap with decoding and network.
- To meet the 95th <120ms E2E: we will need to (a) shorten response lengths for the critical path OR (b) route only classification/short-turn queries to a small, lower-latency model variant (e.g., distilled 7–13B) and reserve the 70B for long-form scoring.

3) Throughput & autoscale
- Sustained 200 qps (per region) with avg 450-token outputs is costly on 70B; multi-tenant batching and KV cache can reduce cost but will increase tail latency without careful scheduling.
- Suggested POC approach: test two routes — (A) latency-sensitive route using a 7–13B low-latency model pinned to a dedicated low-latency pool, (B) quality-sensitive route using the 70B in a separate pool with burst logic and async processing. We'll validate routing policies during the POC.

4) Caching, batching, and SLOs
- Prefix/KV caching is effective if Cliffside has repeated prefixes or assistant-style conversations; we will instrument cache hit rates during POC. Expected token savings up to 25–40% in some flows.
- Continuous batching should be configured with strict max wait thresholds (e.g., 5–10ms) for the latency-sensitive route. We will measure 50/95/99th across both routes.

5) Fallbacks & graceful degradation
- Plan for automatic fallback to hosted lower-cost variants and to regional replicas if Dedicated pool overloaded. Redwood can maintain model-variant compatibility for deterministic fallbacks.

6) Data residency & logging
- For US-only retention, we will put dedicated logs and audit retention in the US region; if Cliffside requires on-prem or VPC private control plane we can scope that in procurement.

7) POC deliverables (technical)
- Benchmarks: baseline latency/throughput for prioritized prompt set (SLA gating).
- Topology sketch: dedicated pools per region + routing policy for latency/quality.
- Cost estimator: expected per-1M-requests cost for both routes.

I'll prepare a short topology diagram and an initial cost estimate for Tue 5/11. If Alex's team can send sample payloads and the prioritized prompt set, I can run a dry-run on a small scale in our staging cluster.
